bluetooth: implement DebugManager for btdispatch DebugManager exposes a D-Bus API to specify the debug verbosity level for dispatcher, newblue, bluez, and kernel. In this patch, only the D-Bus connection and some writing and reading from/to config files (which inits the value of debug verbosity) that has been implemented. The part of printing logs based on these values, is not yet implemented. BUG=chromium:734152 TEST=Do the following. 1) Use the new API dbus-send --system --print-reply --dest=org.chromium.Bluetooth \ /org/chromium/Bluetooth org.chromium.Bluetooth.Debug.SetLevels \ byte:<dispatcher_verbosity> \ byte:<newblue_verbosity> \ byte:<bluez_verbosity> \ byte:<kernel_verbosity> 2) Check the debug conf files on /var/lib/bluetooth/debug.conf contains the actual verbosity level set on step 1. 3) Check the D-Bus property also contains the actual verbosity level. dbus-send --system --dest=org.chromium.Bluetooth --print-reply \ /org/chromium/Bluetooth org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get \ string:org.chromium.Bluetooth.Debug string:<property> Where <property> is one of these below {DispatcherLevel, NewblueLevel, BluezLevel, KernelLevel} Cq-Depend: chromium:1708230,chromium:1728790 Change-Id: I49c679e549d9f3076dcc60e110a25aa7e4387398 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1725690 Tested-by: Archie Pusaka <apusaka@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Sasaka <sonnysasaka@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: crypto: Update for OpenSSL 1.1 OpenSSL 1.1 has made significant non-backwards compatible changes to its API as outlined in: https://wiki.openssl.org/index.php/OpenSSL_1.1.0_Changes This CL adds a libcrypto-compat.[ch] helper layer adapted from the link above. Subsequent CLs convert packages that use libchrome's crypto library (e.g. those in platform2) to be compatible with OpenSSL 1.1 by making use of this common compat layer. This compat layer can be removed once all of Chrome OS has been converted to OpenSSL 1.1+ (crbug.com/984789). In addition to incorporating the stock compat layer: (1) Fix ScopedEVP_MD_CTX since EVP_MD_CTX_destroy has been renamed EVP_MD_CTX_free. (2) Add OpenSSL 1.1 BIO_get/_set() helpers not in the original libcrypto-compat.* files. (3) Add OpenSSL 1.1 HMAC_CTX_new/free() helpers. (4) Add TLS_client_method compat helper This is a Chromium OS local patch because upstream Chromium crypto has already replaced "crypto/scoped_openssl_types.h" with the equivalent BoringSSL scopers. cryptohome: Abort chall-resp mount on ROCA-vuln TPMs Refuse to create/mount challenge-response protected home dirs (a.k.a. smart card login users) when the TPM chip is known to be ROCA-vulnerable. This allows to avoid the unnoticeable security degradation of the strength of the user data protection in the situation where the code can easily detect this weakness. For the background, the challenge-response protection heavily relies on the TPM capabilities. If the TPM is vulnerable and the hardware-backed secrets can be decrypted by an attacker, the only level of the user data protection is the encryption based on a cryptographic signature of a constant per-user salt - which is significantly weaker than the hardware-backed protection. chaps: Use RSA_generate_key_ex() As of OpenSSL 0.9.8, RSA_generate_key() is deprecated in favor of RSA_generate_key_ex(). RSA_generate_key_ex() requires passing in a BIGNUM* exponent, for which we use a crypto::ScopedBIGNUM. Make these changes along with adding proper NULL->nullptr and NULL checks. The end result is no functional change, but better alignment for openssl 1.1 migration.
